# Region map

A region map names what is actually visible in the approved comp before asset production. It is not a page build or an asset approval.

1. Open the exact accepted/proposed reference and record its actual dimensions and revision.
2. Name independently varying regions with stable local IDs, intended medium, source note and actual observed geometry where useful. Keep semantic text/controls distinct from image/material content.
3. Inspect the bounds and foreground/overlap relationships at useful detail; compare grouped and individual crops when existing authorized tools can provide them. A zero-error geometry report would not certify semantic completeness.
4. Correct observed omissions/geometry in a finite pass and retain the exact revision/evidence. A container describes layout extent; it never replaces its children or grants approval.

If the request ends at mapping, return the map observations and unresolved findings at that scope. To continue a prototype, use the current controller and locally adapted new-work procedure; no external command/schema/scaffolder is required.

## Containment

`parentId` identifies an enclosing `container: true` region. Parent and children keep separate IDs and crops. Containment never transfers approval.

## What varies independently

Split regions by what varies independently: content the interface swaps (room photos, products, people), moving parts (a shutter, door or signature interaction), and stable structure (frames, surrounds, ornament). A window can be a surround with a transparent opening, its content image behind it, and separately moving shutters. Overlaps and alpha must match the actual intended composition, not an assumed detector verdict.

## Painted material and semantic interface

Classify observed photos, figures and textures as material requiring suitable permitted assets when that is the accepted promise. Text, controls and interactive geometry need semantic/runtime behavior. A label on a region does not prove its implementation; inspect actual rendered presence and accessibility. Mapping is not asset approval.

Comp crops remain reference evidence unless separately cleared and prepared as permitted production assets. When actual available authorized tools produce crops, bind their source comp/revision and mark them as comp-derived in evidence. No foreign map inspector or inferred approval is required.
